content: Synulox® is a well-recognized veterinary antibiotic that is primarily used to treat infections in the respiratory system, such as the lungs and nasal passages. It is also employed as a broad-spectrum antibiotic. The active components of Synulox are amoxicillin and clavulanic acid, which work together to combat bacterial infections. The combined dosage of the drug is expressed as a total amount, for example, a 500 mg dose consists of 400 mg of amoxicillin and 100 mg of clavulanic acid. Formulations: 1. 500 mg Bolus: These are large, film-coated tablets specifically designed for the treatment of enteritis and navel ill in calves. 2. Intramammary Suspension: This formulation combines Synulox with prednisolone and is intended for intra-mammary infusion. It is used to treat mastitis in lactating cows. 3. Palatable Drops: This is a powdered formulation that requires reconstitution for oral administration. It serves as a broad-spectrum antibiotic for use in dogs and cats. 4. Palatable Tablets: These tablets are available in 50 mg, 250 mg, and 500 mg dosages for oral administration. They are also used as a broad-spectrum antibiotic for dogs and cats. 5. Synulox Ready-To-Use Injection: This is a versatile injectable formulation. It is recommended for: Respiratory tract infections, soft tissue infections, metritis, and mastitis in cattle. Respiratory tract infections, colibacillosis, mastitis, metritis, and agalactia in pigs. Respiratory tract infections, urinary tract infections, and skin and soft tissue infections in dogs and cats. Bacterial Resistance: The issue of bacterial resistance to antibiotics is an increasing concern in veterinary medicine. Clavulanic acid, one of the components of Synulox, functions by inactivating beta-lactamase enzymes, which are a common mechanism of resistance in gram-positive bacteria. Synulox has been reported to be effective against clinical infections caused by Klebsiella species. However, it is not effective against infections caused by Pseudomonas species.
